card.page.delete: Small lowercase text button in a card page's header, shown on hover; opens the delete confirmation. Verb. Keep short.
card.page.kindPlaceholder: Placeholder of the inline editor for a card's `kind` (a free-form subtype like "endpoint"). The leading + means "add". Monospace, small.
card.page.bodyPlaceholder: Placeholder shown where an empty card's markdown body would be; click to start writing. The leading + means "add".
card.section.fields: Small uppercase section heading above a card's frontmatter fields (key/value pairs).
card.section.connections: Small uppercase section heading above the chips linking this card to other cards.
card.fields.add: Small dashed ghost button that adds a frontmatter field. The leading + means "add". Monospace.
card.fields.addPlaceholder: Placeholder of a one-line input where the user types a new field as YAML `key: value`. Keep the colon syntax; translate only the words key/value if your language would.
card.fields.invalidYaml: Error toast: the typed field value is not valid YAML, so nothing was saved. YAML is a format name — do not translate.
card.connections.add: Small dashed ghost button that adds a connection to another card. The leading + means "add". Monospace.
card.connections.addPlaceholder: Placeholder of the input where the user types another card's handle (an uppercase identifier like API-TICKETS). Monospace; uppercase reads as a code token.
card.connections.unknownTarget: Error toast. {handle} is a card identifier (e.g. API-TICKETS) the user typed that does not exist.
card.connections.removeTitle: Tooltip on the small × that removes one connection chip.
card.connections.removeLabel: Screen-reader label for the × button. {handle} is the connected card's identifier.
card.notFound.description: {handle} is a card identifier from the URL, e.g. API-TICKETS.
card.unknownType: Shown when the URL names a card folder that does not exist. {folder} is the raw folder name from the URL (e.g. "apis").
card.typeIntro.count: Small monospace count under a card type's name, e.g. "3 cards".
card.list.ariaLabel: Screen-reader label for the list column of one card type. {type} is the type as an in-sentence noun, e.g. "API endpoint" → "API endpoint cards".
card.list.filterPlaceholder: Placeholder of the search box that filters the card list. Narrow column (~16rem).
card.list.new: Button at the bottom of a card list that creates a card. {type} is the type as an in-sentence lowercase-ish noun ("feature", "API endpoint"). The leading + means "add".
card.list.empty: Shown in a card list that has no cards of this type yet.
card.create.title: Dialog title. {type} is the card type as an in-sentence noun ("feature", "API endpoint", "database table").
card.create.titleNoType: Dialog title when the type is unknown.
card.create.description: Help line under the dialog title. A handle is the card's identifier (e.g. API-TICKETS); the type prefix is the part before the first dash.
card.create.handleLabel: Form label. "Handle" is Constellation's term for a card's unique identifier (e.g. API-TICKETS).
card.create.handlePlaceholder: Example handle suffix typed after a fixed prefix like "API-". Must stay uppercase A–Z/0–9/dashes; you may keep it as-is.
card.create.nameLabel: Form label for the card's optional human-readable display name.
card.create.optional: Faint tag after the Name label meaning the field may be left empty.
card.create.namePlaceholder: Placeholder of the display-name input: a short description of the card.
card.create.preview: Live preview line under the form. {handle} (shown bold) is the handle that will be created, e.g. API-NEW-TICKET.
card.create.errorInvalid: Inline form error. Handles may only contain A–Z, 0–9 and dashes — keep those characters literally.
card.delete.title: Confirmation dialog title. {handle} is the card identifier.
card.delete.confirm: Destructive confirm button in the delete dialog.
card.delete.referenced.single: Delete dialog text. {handle} is the card; {handles} is the ONE card connected to it.
card.delete.referenced.multiple: Delete dialog text. {handle} is the card; {handles} is a comma-separated list of two or more cards connected to it.
card.delete.referencedAt.single: As card.delete.referenced.single, plus {path}: the card's file path (e.g. api/API-TICKETS.md).
card.delete.referencedAt.multiple: As card.delete.referenced.multiple, plus {path}: the card's file path (e.g. api/API-TICKETS.md).
card.delete.unreferencedAt: {path} is the card's file path (e.g. api/API-TICKETS.md).
card.delete.doneDangling.single: Toast after deleting {handle}. {handles} is the ONE card whose connection now points at nothing (conjugate for a singular subject).
card.delete.doneDangling.multiple: Toast after deleting {handle}. {handles} is a comma-separated list of two or more cards whose connections now point at nothing.
edit.hint: Tiny monospace hint under a multi-line inline editor. Keep the key glyphs ⌘↩ and esc; translate only "save" and "cancel". Keep it short — one line.
edit.emptyPlaceholder: Faint italic placeholder for an empty editable value.
edit.toast.stale: Error toast: the card file was changed by something else since it was loaded, so the save was refused and the page reloaded.
edit.toast.readonly: Error toast: the viewer server runs in read-only mode.
edit.toast.saveFailed: Fallback error toast when the server gave no message.
edit.toast.syncPoint: Success toast. {sha} is a short git commit id (8 hex characters).
style.guide.emptyTitle: Empty-state title. STYLE is a card type prefix — keep it as-is.
style.guide.emptyDescription: Empty-state help. style/ is a folder name and "tokens"/"category" are field names — keep them as-is.
style.fontStyles: Small heading above a list mapping font token names to CSS font stacks.
style.specimen.uppercase: Tiny label above a row of A–Z sample letters in a font specimen.
style.specimen.lowercase: Tiny label above a row of a–z sample letters in a font specimen.
style.specimen.numbers: Tiny label above the digits 0–9 in a font specimen.
style.specimen.characters: Tiny label above a row of punctuation/symbol characters in a font specimen.
style.typeScale.sample: Sample sentence rendered at each size of a type scale. Use your language's pangram or any natural sentence of similar length.
